sst_write_governance.policy: SST is READ-ONLY by default and technically enforced in the pbswi automations: airtable_writer.py raises AirTableSafetyError on any write. Writes require an explicit allow_tables override plus documented user authorization.
sst_write_governance.only_sanctioned_bulk_path: Templated SST batch CREATE (section 3a), governed by C1-C5. C3 is create-only: it never updates an existing SST record.
sst_write_governance.cardigan_status: Cardigan's patch_sst_record (mcp_server/server.py) PATCHes SST directly with the API key and does NOT route through airtable_writer.py. It therefore bypasses the safety layer entirely -- no allowlist check, no rollback log, no collision guard. Every Cardigan publish is an UPDATE, which is exactly what the one sanctioned path excludes.
sst_write_governance.implication: The publish path needs documented authorization before it can ship, independent of any field mapping.

format.rule: Read-modify-write an owned block. Never replace the whole field.
format.on_write: If exactly one ordered marker pair is present (start before end), replace only what lies between them. If no markers are present, APPEND the block after existing content with one blank line of separation. Anything else (one marker, end before start, multiple pairs): refuse and surface for a human. Never touch bytes outside the markers.
format.concurrency: AirTable has no compare-and-swap. Use the commit_sst_edits mechanism: re-fetch immediately before PATCH and abort if the field changed since the proposal. This narrows the race window but does not close it.
format.round_trip: richText is markdown-flavoured ('---' can render as a rule). The first implementation must write, read back, and confirm the markers survive; marker matching should tolerate whitespace/escaping changes.
format.precedent: Mirrors the AIRTABLE_SYNC_START/END owned-region convention in pbswi's sync_airtable_to_obsidian.py. Plain-text markers rather than HTML comments, because AirTable richText renders comments literally.
format.contents: The chapter list, and the transcript link when one exists.
format.single_writer: Phases never write AirTable. The transcript link (formatter) and chapters (timestamp) have independent producers and would race for the same block if each wrote on completion -- the later write would erase the earlier one. The block is assembled and written ONCE by the publish step from current job state, so a re-publish rewrites it wholesale and is idempotent. Matches the map's stage 5: publish is a single universal action, not a per-phase side effect.

platform_notes_contract.blocking_governance: Field answered, write posture open. As of this audit (2026-08-28) pbswi issue #142 ('Confirm with Lisa: OK to use SST Platform Notes for automation metadata stamps?') was open and untouched since 2026-07-02. Update 2026-10-21: the field question was answered on 2026-09-01 -- Platform Notes is a Digital Team field, already used for automation timestamps and chapter lists. Still open: the base owner's sign-off on automated SST writes and the conditions on Cardigan's write path, tracked in pbswi-ops#9; shipping waits on that. 'target_identified_pending_authorization' is not a go-ahead: Platform Notes is not in WRITABLE_FIELDS, and adding it is a separate, gated allowlist change.
